sections.title: The maize genus
sections.text: Zea is a genus of grasses native to Mexico and Central America. The plate depicts cultivated maize, Zea mays: a tall annual with broad leaves, a terminal male tassel and female ears on the stem. Depending on cultivar and growing conditions, maize plants may exceed 3 m; the image represents maize rather than the other Zea species.

sections.title: Ears and kernels
sections.text: Silks emerge from each developing ear and receive pollen from the tassel; the kernels are the grains. Sweet-corn cultivars are eaten fresh or cooked, while field, popcorn and ornamental forms have different uses. This food use applies to cultivated maize grain, not automatically to every part or wild relative.
